title: Uncontrolled Subprocess Spawning via OpencodeModelRegistry
root_cause: Three code paths (discoverAtStartup, refreshFromCli, runBlockingRefresh) spawn `opencode` subprocess using ProcessBuilder without PATH validation, binary verification, or working directory isolation. Timeout via waitFor + destroyForcibly can leave orphaned processes. Silent empty-list fallback on failure loses model governance.
reproduction_steps: Place a malicious `opencode` script earlier in PATH than the real CLI binary
Start the Friday server
Observe that the malicious binary executes with full JVM process permissions during `discoverAtStartup()`

title: Session State Race Condition Across Concurrent SSE Streams
root_cause: ActiveEventBridge, ActiveSessionManager, and chat event emitter all use userId as the key with overwrite semantics. Multiple concurrent SSE connections from the same Firebase user cause event misrouting, session info overwrite, and progressive database saves targeting the wrong session.
reproduction_steps: Obtain a valid Firebase token for a test user
Open two concurrent SSE connections to `/chat/stream` with same token
Trigger an approval-requiring tool in the first session
Observe the ApprovalRequested event arriving in the second session's stream

title: Unbounded SSE Event Buffer with No Backpressure
root_cause: The LLM streaming pipeline (Flow.collect -> EventEmitter -> SSE send) has no backpressure mechanism. Fast LLM generation can overflow memory via in-flight event accumulation, unbounded thinking trace growth, and raw response sample StringBuilder with no size cap. SSE disconnect detection is not propagated to stop the Flow collector.
reproduction_steps: Send a query that triggers a long generation (e.g., 'write a 50-page essay')
Disconnect the SSE client mid-stream
Observe server memory growing as Flow.collect continues accumulating events

title: Approval Resolution Not Scoped to Authenticated User
root_cause: POST /api/v1/chat/events/approval resolves approvals by toolId only, without verifying that the requesting user owns the approval. ApprovalRegistry is a global ConcurrentHashMap with no per-user scoping. Any authenticated user who knows a toolId can approve or deny another user's pending tool execution.
reproduction_steps: User A triggers a tool requiring approval (e.g., device action)
User A's SSE stream emits ApprovalRequested with toolId 'abc-123'
User B (different Firebase account) sends POST /api/v1/chat/events/approval with toolId='abc-123' and approved=true
The tool executes for User A despite User B providing the approval

title: LlmCacheKey Uses ByteArray in Data Class Breaking Equals/HashCode
root_cause: LlmCacheKey contains List<LlmMessage> which has a List<ByteArray>? field. ByteArray on JVM uses referential identity (not structural equality) for equals()/hashCode(). The LLM response cache silently never hits for any request with image attachments, and hash computation is O(n) on ByteArray content for no benefit.
reproduction_steps: Send query A with an image to the chat endpoint
Send the identical query A with the same image again
Observe that the cache log shows no cache hit (the second request processes fully)

title: Interrupt Endpoint Does Not Cancel Running Agent Coroutines
root_cause: POST /chat/interrupt clears the session checkpoint but has no mechanism to cancel the running ServerAgent coroutine. No Job handle is stored for the agent execution. Between the checkpoint being cleared and the agent's next loop iteration checking it, one additional tool call can execute without protection.
reproduction_steps: Send a deep research query that triggers a long chain of tool calls
Immediately send POST /chat/interrupt with the session ID
Observe that the agent may still execute 1-2 more tool calls before the loop condition detects the cleared checkpoint

title: SQL Migration Parser Desync on Dollar-Quoted Strings
root_cause: The SQL statement splitter uses a naive $$ toggle state machine that can desync if dollar-quoted strings contain $$ in comments or string literals. If desynced, statement boundaries are misidentified and SQL execution errors are silently swallowed by the catch(Exception) block.
reproduction_steps: Add a migration SQL file containing a function body with a comment containing '$$'
Observe only on careful inspection: the function body straddling a split boundary causes a SQL syntax error that is caught and logged at debug level

title: ThinkingStorageManager Mutex Doesn't Cover DB Write
root_cause: The ThinkingStorageManager mutex protects only the in-memory block list, but the database write of the thinking trace happens outside the mutex. A rapid tool result arriving between the mutex release and DB write causes the stored thinking trace to be stale.
reproduction_steps: Send a query that triggers two rapid tool calls in succession
Examine the stored thinking trace in the database
The final thinking trace may not include the second tool call's output

title: POST /chat/events Accepts Arbitrary Deserialized ClientEvent Types
root_cause: The /chat/events endpoint deserializes ClientEvent sealed class with classDiscriminator, accepting any subtype. The else branch silently ignores unhandled types, but ToolResult events are written to chat history without validation beyond the deserialization. An authenticated user could inject fabricated tool results into their own conversation history.
reproduction_steps: Authenticate as a valid Firebase user
POST /chat/events?sessionId=abc with body: {"type":"tool_result","commandId":"x","result":"FAKE DATA","isError":false,"timestamp":0}
The injected data appears in the conversation history loaded on the next agent request

title: HTML-Entity Sanitization Irrelevant for JSON API Architecture
root_cause: InputValidation.sanitizeInput() encodes HTML entities (< -> < etc.) and checks for XSS patterns. The application uses JSON serialization + native Compose UI rendering, where HTML entity encoding has no effect and XSS patterns are not exploitable. The sanitization is architecturally irrelevant.
reproduction_steps: Send a query with <script>alert('xss')</script> to the chat endpoint
Observe that the input is either rejected by validateQuery (if it matches injection patterns) or passed through
The stored value in JSON format cannot inject JavaScript into native Compose UI rendering

title: sessionMessageCount Map Grows Without Eviction
root_cause: OpencodeLlmProvider.sessionMessageCount is a ConcurrentHashMap<String, Int> with no cleanup, TTL, or eviction policy. Each daemon session creates a persistent entry. Sustained session churn causes unbounded map growth.
reproduction_steps: Rapidly create and destroy chat sessions (e.g., script 10,000 requests)
Observe sessionMessageCount growing monotonically without removal
Each entry persists until JVM restart
